description: Figure 3 is a line chart titled "Ablation Study on HateXplain Dataset," which illustrates the performance of different model variants of MS-FSLHate across three metrics: precision, recall, and F1-score. The horizontal x-axis, labeled "Model Variants," lists five categories: "Full model (Ours)," "w/o Prompt," "w/o Augmentation," "w/o Attention," and "w/o Prompt & Augmentation." The vertical y-axis, labeled "Metric (%)," ranges from 58 to 66, with major gridlines at 58, 60, 62, 64, and 66. Three distinct lines represent the metrics: a purple line for Precision, a blue line for Recall, and a brown line for F1-score, as indicated by the legend in the lower-left corner. The Full model (Ours) achieves the highest scores: 65.45% for Precision, 65.78% for Recall, and 65.56% for F1-score. Removing the prompt (w/o Prompt) causes Precision to drop to 61.06% and Recall to 59.64%, while F1-score falls to 60.16%. Removing augmentation (w/o Augmentation) results in Precision of 62.22%, Recall of 63.75%, and F1-score of 62.63%. Removing attention (w/o Attention) leads to Precision of 64.06%, Recall of 59.17%, and F1-score of 59.67%. The variant without both prompt and augmentation (w/o Prompt & Augmentation) shows Precision at 65.44%, Recall at 56.82%, and F1-score at 57.74%. The chart visually depicts how each ablation affects the three performance metrics, with the lines showing varying trends of decline or relative stability across the different model configurations.
